findings.title: Denial cache ignores newly granted permissions
findings.body: Check returns Allowed=false as soon as a denial-cache entry exists for (namespace, subject, action, name, parent), before consulting either the permission cache or the database. Entries are written for every deny and kept for shortCacheTTL (30s), and nothing deletes them when a role, team, or creator grant later adds that scope. A user who was denied on a dashboard or folder they then create or are granted will keep getting denied until TTL, which is the failure this PR is meant to fix. The same sticky deny is recorded when checkPermission fails only because the folder tree cache is stale, so a parent-folder grant on a just-created child stays denied even after the tree would have allowed it.

findings.title: Denial cache key aliases different resources
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey joins name and parent with '_' and both values are UIDs that may themselves contain underscores. Distinct pairs such as name "a_b" / parent "c" and name "a" / parent "b_c" produce the same key. A cached deny for one pair is then treated as a deny for the other, so Check can reject a resource the user is allowed to access for up to 30 seconds.

findings.title: List still serves a stale permission cache
findings.body: List returns immediately when getCachedIdentityPermissions hits, and never re-reads the DB if the cached scope map is missing a dashboard or folder created after the entry was stored. Check was changed to requery on a negative cache result; List was not. Creators and users who just received access will not see the new resource in list/fetch results until shortCacheTTL expires.

findings.title: Remote AuthZ client still caches decisions for 30s
findings.body: Only the in-proc client is switched to NoopCache. newRemoteRBACClient still wraps the gRPC client in a local cache with a 30s expiry. Cloud/remote callers therefore keep returning the previous allow/deny for a newly created dashboard or folder until that client entry expires, so the server-side requery never runs and the reported creator access bug remains in that mode.
